findings.title: Validate copied source contents against the admitted Git snapshot before copying
findings.description: prepare() inventories the current live source and checks only that its private copy equals those current bytes. The subsequent copied-vcpkg-identity command at lines 185-187 resolves HEAD and HEAD^{tree}, which do not attest working-tree bytes, executable modes, or extra untracked/ignored inputs. The frozen contract protects the vcpkg executable but contains no complete admitted source inventory, and the reused preservation inventory has no vcpkg source records. A fresh invocation can therefore accept a changed source tree while reporting the pinned commit/tree.
findings.executed_evidence: The actual AST-extracted prepare() and prefix_inventory() accepted all three drift variants: changed tracked-file bytes, changed tracked executable mode, and an unexpected untracked file. All retained the same valid loose Git commit/tree objects and bootstrap binary SHA256, and the copied sources preserved each drift. A clean control also passed. No Git or vcpkg subprocess was invoked.
findings.requested_change: Bind a complete admitted source inventory in the contract and compare the fresh inventory before copy. Derive its tracked file contents and executable modes from the pinned Git tree; allow only explicitly qualified bootstrap outputs, including the hash-bound vcpkg binary and empty disable-metrics marker. Preserve the existing no-symlink, alternates and common-dir rejections, copy equality and final source preservation.

focused_controls.preservation: all 10 frozen unit inputs unchanged before and after controls and at packaging

static_review: Reviewed the actual four maintained unit files and frozen receipts, root onboarding/AGENTS guidance and the applicable accepted decisions and plan status.

Reviewed private roots, command arguments, unchanged HOME check, selected exact host tools and named environment probes; the command scope is fetch cmake/ninja only, with no configure, dependency build or compiler invocation.

The sandbox profile denies writes except the private operation root and /dev/null, and denies network. The positive write and outside-write/symlink/network denial controls precede vcpkg fetch. DENIED controls accept only EPERM/EACCES, with explicit return code 73; connection refusal or timeout would propagate.

The reused native runner is hash-bound and passes the explicit lease descriptor; documented inherited descriptors are 0, 1, 2 and the lease. Canonical lease/census and existing runner cleanup contracts were reviewed by reference, not re-executed.
The new wrapper preserves unexpected failures and the outer BaseException/finally paths save FAIL state and preservation receipts. The eight new wrapper mocks passed.
Original Claude marketplace acceptance bytes match all 19 baseline records; this is static preservation evidence only.
not_run: earlier triplet or cleanup test batteries
limitations: This is a preparation review. Native macOS confinement and the intended vcpkg tool-selection operation remain UNVERIFIED.
The source controls use private synthetic sources and decoded Git objects; they do not assert that the current real source checkout is dirty.
ownership: No maintained, global or real source files were changed. Reviewer writes are confined to the private review directory.
